facts.content: Patient has been wheezy and experiencing shortness of breath for 2 days.
Symptoms started after house-cleaning with dust exposure and began approximately 1 hour post-exposure.
facts.source_text: Onset after house‐cleaning with dust exposure; began ~1 h post-exposure, progressive, worse at night

facts.content: There is no chest pain or dizziness.
Patient had childhood asthma and occasionally used an inhaler for exertion.
facts.source_text: PMH: childhood asthma (occasional exertional use of inhaler)

facts.content: Patient has an unused asthma inhaler, details not given.
facts.source_text: Meds: has unused asthma inhaler (details not given)

facts.content: Patient does not take regular antihistamines.
Patient denies known drug allergies and suspects sensitivity to dust.
facts.source_text: Allergies: denies known drug allergies; suspects dust sensitivity

facts.content: Wheeze and shortness of breath are likely due to an asthma flare or dust-allergy-induced bronchospasm.
facts.source_text: Wheeze/SOB – likely asthma flare vs dust-allergy–induced bronchospasm

facts.content: Advised to try over-the-counter antihistamines en route to general practitioner.
facts.source_text: Advise OTC antihistamine trial en route to GP

facts.content: Same-day review by general practitioner for pulse-ox, lung exam, and possibly peak flow.
facts.source_text: Same-day GP review for pulse-ox, lung exam, ± peak flow

facts.content: Bring existing inhaler to general practitioner; GP to consider SABA use and oral steroids after assessment.
facts.source_text: Bring existing inhaler; GP to consider SABA use and oral steroids after assessment

facts.content: Letter sent to general practitioner via app.
facts.source_text: Letter to GP sent via app

facts.content: Patient advised on red-flag symptoms and to seek urgent care if condition worsens.
